The widespread adoption of smartphones has driven a surge in mobile application usage, prompting the need for more personalized user experiences. To achieve this, developers are increasingly leveraging user context to deliver tailored content. This paper introduces a new framework designed to capture and utilize user context within mobile settings. It proposes a context-aware architecture that enables mobile apps to access contextual data from other applications, thereby enhancing the ability to present customized content. The framework's viability is demonstrated through a case study involving a photo-sharing service that utilizes persistent context values from a music player to suggest personalized photo albums.

This study introduces a novel 3D pose estimation framework designed to deliver real-time performance on resource-constrained hardware. The approach employs a dual-branch architecture that processes images and skeletal data in parallel, utilizing a multi-scale feature extraction module to capture scale-invariant representations. Furthermore, the system incorporates a dedicated attention mechanism to enhance the discriminative power of these features. Experimental results indicate that the model attains state-of-the-art accuracy on the CMU Panoptic Kinetics dataset, surpassing existing methods. Additionally, the framework demonstrates robust generalization capabilities across various datasets and exhibits resilience against occlusions.

The AstroSat mission, launched in 2015, carries the Cadmium-Zinc-Telluride (CZT) imaging spectrometer, which utilizes collimators to restrict its field of view to approximately 10 arcminutes. This design choice was intended to enhance the instrument's sensitivity and reduce background noise. This study details the flux measurements of 11 X-ray point sources—specifically Sgr A*, Sco X-1, Cyg X-1, and 4U 1608-72—obtained with the AstroSat CZT collimated instrument. Flux values were determined using the AstroSat's onboard data processing pipeline, which applies a background subtraction method based on the source's position within the field of view. The analysis reveals that Cyg X-1 and Sco X-1 are the only sources for which reliable flux measurements were obtained. The derived flux for Cyg X-1 is $1.03 \pm 0.13$ photons cm$^{-2}$ s$^{-1}$, while Sco X-1 is measured at $0.13 \pm 0.02$ photons cm$^{-2}$ s$^{-1}$. These results align closely with the values reported in the literature.

Blockchain protocols are categorized based on their permissioned versus permissionless nature, as well as their underlying consensus mechanisms. This paper introduces a framework for evaluating blockchain protocols by defining a set of requirements for permissioned systems and selecting 14 prominent real-world examples to assess against these criteria. The study details the permissioned protocol's specifications, outlines the selection rationale, presents the assessment outcomes, and concludes with a summary of the work.

This study examines the impact of a non-standard initial condition for the Higgs field on the renormalization group (RG) evolution of the instability scale. We derive the resulting constraints on the Higgs mass within extended Standard Model frameworks, specifically accounting for the interplay between the instability scale and the Higgs mass. Our analysis reveals that the instability scale's bound on the Higgs mass is notably relaxed when the initial Higgs value exceeds the standard critical value of approximately $10^{10}$ GeV. Furthermore, we explore the consequences of a high-energy instability scale for the stability of the vacuum, the cosmological constant, and the fine-tuning problem.

This study demonstrates that the solution to the Hamilton-Jacobi equation within Carnot groups satisfies the $\mathfrak{p}$-Talagrand inequality, provided the $\mathfrak{p}$-entropy is governed by a sub-Laplacian. Furthermore, we establish a connection linking this result to the validity of a Poincaré inequality under the same sub-Laplacian-driven $\mathfrak{p}$-entropy metric.

This paper introduces a novel estimator, termed Exponentially Weighted Divergence (EWD), which serves as a robust alternative to the established Density Power Divergence (DPD) family. The EWD estimator is defined by its computational simplicity, relying on a single kernel density estimate, whereas the DPD estimator requires calculating two distinct estimates. Empirical evaluations demonstrate that the EWD estimator achieves performance comparable to DPD while maintaining similar levels of robustness. Additionally, the study derives the asymptotic distribution of the EWD estimator and confirms these findings through simulation.

This study introduces a novel method for segmenting static and motion-oriented regions within an image, leveraging a newly developed algorithm that identifies pixels exhibiting significant movement. By applying this method to a reference image alongside a target one, the approach effectively distinguishes static areas from those that have changed. Furthermore, the technique is utilized to estimate the position of a robot.

Periodic orbits are fundamental to the semiclassical approximation of the Riemann zeta function's characteristic polynomial, yet their self-intersections complicate the analysis of coefficient variances. This study examines a specific class of periodic orbits, known as "simple loops," which are free of self-intersections. We demonstrate that the variance of coefficients corresponding to these simple loops is approximately one-eighth of the total number of such loops. This finding aligns with the prediction of random matrix theory, which posits that the variance of each coefficient should equal one-half of the count of periodic orbits of matching length.

The OGLE-IV survey, which targets the Galactic bulge, has identified 1,053 periodic variable stars that are either eclipsing binaries or nebular variables (NEB). This study details the classification process for these objects, which relies on a combination of light curve analysis, photometric data, and spectroscopic observations. The final categorization includes 410 eclipsing binaries and 643 NEB variables. Furthermore, we have established a robust classification framework that effectively distinguishes these periodic variables from non-periodic ones.

This study addresses the problem of identifying both the closest negative imaginary (NI) and the closest non-negative imaginary (NNI) systems relative to a given linear time invariant (LTI) system. While the nearest NNI system can be derived directly from the given system, determining the nearest NS system presents a more significant challenge. We formulate this nearest NS problem as a convex optimization task and introduce an iterative algorithm to solve it. Numerical examples demonstrate the efficacy of our proposed approach.

Continual learning (CL) represents a pivotal area in machine learning, focusing on systems capable of mastering new tasks while retaining knowledge of prior ones. This study introduces End-to-End Automatic Speech Recognition (E2ESR) as a novel domain for CL research. We evaluate three distinct CL strategies: (1) a method utilizing a dynamic expansion of the model's width, (2) a technique employing a fixed sparse architecture, and (3) a hybrid approach combining both methods. Our findings indicate that the top-performing CL technique achieves a 20% improvement over standard fine-tuning for new tasks, while maintaining performance parity on previous tasks. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the sparse architecture method offers a practical balance, delivering a 10% boost for new tasks alongside only a 5% reduction in performance for old tasks.

Code-switching, the intermixing of two or more languages within a single utterance, is prevalent in social media communication. This phenomenon presents significant challenges for sentiment analysis, primarily due to the scarcity of labeled datasets and the absence of effective modeling strategies. This study introduces a code-switching sentiment analysis framework for the English-Finnish language pair, utilizing a pre-trained transformer model. Our approach employs a multilingual transformer architecture that leverages extensive pre-training to enhance the representation of code-switched text. We further demonstrate that fine-tuning the model on a small, curated dataset yields superior performance compared to using the model in its pre-trained state. Experimental results indicate that our method achieves an F1-score of 0.71 on the test set.

This study examines a three-loop neutrino seesaw model that generates neutrino masses through radiative corrections. The framework incorporates a scalar leptoquark ($S_3$) and a scalar singlet ($\phi$), both of which emerge as new particles detectable at the LHC. The $S_3$ leptoquark can decay into a lepton and a quark pair, while the $\phi$ scalar mixes with the Standard Model Higgs boson. Our analysis reveals that the $S_3$ leptoquark is constrained by existing LHC data, whereas the $\phi$ scalar is predicted to be lighter than 129 GeV. Furthermore, the mixing between $\phi$ and the Higgs boson is bounded by the absence of observed excesses in the $B_s \to \mu^+\mu^-$ decay rate and the $B \to K\nu\bar\nu$ process. Consequently, the model predicts a $\phi$ mass below 110 MeV. Additionally, the $S_3$ leptoquark is identified as a viable dark matter candidate, with its relic density falling within the range favored by current cosmological observations.

Product-based Neural Networks (PNNs) are designed to capture interactions among categorical variables by encoding them as lookup tables within embedding layers. This study empirically investigates the impact of PNN architecture on model performance, specifically examining how the arrangement of dense and embedding layers influences predictive accuracy. Our findings indicate that an optimal PNN structure resembles a feedforward neural network, where the count of dense layers roughly equals the count of dense fields in the input. We further validate these insights through a case study on a customer churn prediction task.

This study examines active transmitting beamforming design for a hybrid active transmitting beamforming (ATB) and intelligent reflecting surface (IRS) system. We address the challenge of jointly optimizing transmit beamforming vectors and IRS phase shifts to maximize the minimum rate of all users, subject to a total transmit power limit. We first analyze the ideal scenario with perfect channel state information (CSI) and subsequently address the more realistic case involving CSI uncertainty. In the context of uncertainty, we introduce a robust counterpart formulation that ensures the minimum rate constraint holds for any channel realization within the defined uncertainty set. We subsequently develop an efficient algorithm to solve this robust problem, demonstrating its performance through numerical simulations. Our results indicate that while CSI uncertainty significantly impacts minimum rate performance, the proposed robust design effectively mitigates these effects. Furthermore, we observe that the optimal active transmitting beamforming strategy in robust design differs from that in the perfect CSI scenario.

Branch prediction is a critical component of modern CPUs, and while traditional methods like static and dynamic branch predictors have been extensively studied, dynamic approaches leveraging deep learning algorithms have recently gained significant attention. This paper introduces a dynamic branch prediction model that integrates a deep neural network with a history-based mechanism. The proposed methodology utilizes a deep neural network to forecast outcomes for recent branch instructions, relying on a specialized history buffer to capture the execution patterns of these recent operations. Furthermore, the study evaluates the model's effectiveness by benchmarking it against several existing branch prediction strategies.

This paper introduces a deep convolutional neural network designed to autonomously manage a camera system. The system's primary objective is to track a specific target within a defined area, adjusting the camera pan, tilt, and zoom settings to maintain the target in the image frame. Unlike conventional approaches that rely on image processing algorithms, this method leverages the deep convolutional neural network to identify the target's position, thereby enabling precise camera orientation. Experimental results demonstrate that the system achieves a 100% detection rate for the target. Furthermore, the proposed framework is highly adaptable, allowing for the seamless integration of various camera configurations and control mechanisms.

This study examines the one-dimensional SOS model with a ferromagnetic interaction and a boundary field, specifically focusing on the model's phase diagram. We demonstrate that when the bulk critical temperature is sufficiently low, there exist intervals within the parameter space where non-normalisable boundary states occur. Furthermore, we establish that these boundary states are linked to the emergence of a phase that exhibits both long-range order and a finite correlation length. We also identify the critical connection between the presence of such non-normalisable boundary states and the occurrence of a phase transition.

This study introduces a novel experimental approach to characterize entangled two-photon resonance energy transfer (E2P) using a single-molecule technique. By monitoring the fluorescence emission of individual molecules within a 2D plane, we successfully visualized the spatial distribution of E2P interactions. The E2P rate coefficient, denoted as $K_{E2P}$, was determined from the fluorescence decay of single molecules, revealing a broad spectrum of values ranging from $10^{-10}$ to $10^{-3} \, \text{s}^{-1}$. These results demonstrate that the proposed method offers a highly sensitive means for investigating weak E2P interactions.

We calculate the strong coupling constants for the $D_s$ and $D$ mesons interacting with $D^*$ and $\Lambda_b$ baryons using light-cone QCD sum rules. The outcomes of these calculations align closely with those derived from the perturbative QCD approach and the unitarity method.

The anomalous results from short-baseline neutrino oscillation experiments, including LSND and MiniBooNE, are examined. We demonstrate that the 3+1 neutrino model, which is the standard explanation for these phenomena, is incompatible with recent data from IceCube. Furthermore, we show that the anomalies can alternatively be explained by a 3+3 neutrino model, which is consistent with IceCube constraints. We also analyze the long-baseline anomaly and conclude that the current oscillation paradigm, based on three neutrino states, is insufficient to account for it.

To advance causal inference within the framework of randomized experiments, it is essential to design observational studies that can credibly estimate causal effects. This paper demonstrates that inverse propensity weighting (IPW) in observational research can be conceptualized as a weighted sample mean derived from linear regression. This perspective reveals that regression methods can assign weights to units based on their characteristics, thereby guiding the selection of treatment and control groups for optimal study design. We propose a framework for experimental design that leverages these regression-derived weights to construct balanced subsets of units, ensuring that the resulting samples are representative of the full population. Our approach is validated through both simulation studies and a real-world application involving the analysis of observational data from the Human Genome Diversity Project.

This study examines the impact of voltage source converters (VSCs) on mitigating and amplifying oscillations within power systems. By employing a two-machine system, the work analyzes how VSCs can dampen or exacerbate oscillations and explores the control strategies required to achieve this. The investigation covers both weakly and strongly coupled scenarios, with analysis conducted using both time-domain and frequency-domain methods. The paper concludes by detailing the control parameters that dictate a VSC's influence on system oscillations.

We examine the quantum characteristics of light emitted by a thermally excited atomic ensemble within the single-atom limit of the dipole approximation, specifically focusing on scenarios involving two-atom and three-atom decays. The emitted light displays sub-Poissonian photon statistics, demonstrating non-classical behavior. We derive a quantum master equation for the atomic ensemble that accounts for both collective and individual decay pathways. Utilizing this framework, we calculate the second-order correlation function for the emitted radiation and identify a photon bunching effect, which manifests as a peak value of $g^{(2)}(0)=2$ in the two-atom regime.

This study examines the stability of kink solutions within nonlinear field theories featuring internal modes. We establish that internal modes invariably destabilize kinks, with the instability stemming from the emergence of a complex eigenvalue near zero as the internal mode frequency approaches zero. Furthermore, we offer a precise formula for calculating the internal mode frequency, enabling prediction of the instability onset. This finding is validated through analytical solutions in specific scenarios and numerical tests across various models.

Generalized parton distributions (GPDs) are essential for understanding high-energy hadron production and the internal structure of nucleons. This study examines the connection between GPDs and the amplitude of the $2 \to 2$ scattering process involving a nucleon and a virtual photon. We demonstrate that the connection between these two quantities is governed by a specific kinematic configuration. This framework enables the extraction of GPDs from data collected at future high-energy colliders.

Text classification is a fundamental natural language processing application, yet it remains susceptible to adversarial attacks. This study introduces a novel defense mechanism that employs discrete noise injection to disrupt the training model's decision boundary. We utilize a specialized discrete noise distribution that alters the input distribution, thereby shifting the decision boundary to a new position. We present a method for calculating the optimal noise distribution parameters that maximizes the minimum adversarial accuracy. Experiments across multiple datasets demonstrate that the resulting noisy model exhibits significantly higher robustness against various adversarial attacks.

Accurate polyp detection is essential for endoscopic procedures, yet the small size of these polyp regions and the scarcity of spatial context hinder precise segmentation. To address this, we introduce a novel channel-aware attention mechanism designed to aggregate features from various endoscopic video frames. This approach leverages the temporal dimension to enhance feature aggregation, thereby improving detection accuracy. Specifically, we propose a Channel-aware Attention Network (CANet) that integrates this mechanism into a multi-scale feature fusion module. Experimental results demonstrate that our model achieves state-of-the-art performance on the MICCAI 2017 EndoNet dataset, surpassing existing methods by 0.71% in Dice coefficient and 0.71% in Intersection over Union.

This work introduces a sequential sampling technique that allows for controlled spreading in the drawn sequence, adjustable via a user-defined parameter. The degree of spread can be expanded or contracted at each sampling step, with the method demonstrated to exhibit asymptotic normality. We provide simulation results to illustrate the approach's performance.

The rp-process, occurring during Type-I X-ray bursts, is characterized by the rapid proton capture of unstable nuclei. This study utilizes a Monte Carlo framework to simulate the process, incorporating nuclear reaction rates derived from both experimental data and theoretical models. The analysis focuses on the 2000–20000 K temperature range, which is typical for X-ray bursts, and examines the impact of uncertainties in nuclear rates on the resulting isotopic abundances. The findings indicate that approximately 10% of the rp-process flux bypasses the waiting point $^{56}$Ni, with a similar fraction (around 9%) of the flux reaching the subsequent waiting point $^{56}$Zn. The study further explores how variations in nuclear reaction rates influence the abundance of these specific waiting points.

This study extends our previous work on the moduli space of $p$-divisible groups to incorporate a $p$-divisible lattice of arbitrary height, thereby establishing a framework for analyzing the moduli of $p$-divisible lattices modulo $p$-divisible lattices of arbitrary height. We demonstrate that the moduli space of $p$-divisible lattices modulo $p$-divisible lattices of arbitrary height is smooth and irreducible, with a unique irreducible component whose closure contains the flat part of the moduli space of $p$-divisible lattices modulo $p$-divisible lattices of arbitrary height. Furthermore, we show that the flat part of the moduli space of $p$-divisible lattices modulo $p$-divisible lattices of arbitrary height is a union of irreducible components, each of which is a torsion coset of the moduli space of $p$-divisible lattices modulo $p$-divisible lattices of arbitrary height. We also establish that the irreducible components of the moduli space of $p$-divisible lattices modulo $p$-divisible lattices of arbitrary height are smooth and irreducible, with a unique irreducible component whose closure contains the flat part of the moduli space of $p$-divisible lattices modulo $p$-divisible lattices of arbitrary height. Finally, we show that the

Recent Very High Energy (HEV) gamma-ray observations from the H.E.S.S. observatory have significantly refined our understanding of the Milky Way's gamma-ray sources. This study utilizes a new, high-resolution model of the galactic diffuse gamma-ray emission to analyze H.E.S.S. data from the Galactic center region. By employing a Bayesian inference framework, we derive posterior distributions for the key parameters of the H.E.S.S. spectral energy model. These results are then used to forecast the expected counts for the upcoming Cherenkov Telescope Array (CTA).

This study examines the nonequilibrium dynamics of a diffusion model featuring nonlocal boundary conditions, where the interaction kernel is defined by the domain's geometry. We establish a connection between this broad class of nonlocal problems and the classical local Cauchy problem for linear kinetic equations. Leveraging this link, we derive a new representation formula for the solution of the diffusion model and prove the existence of the weak solution.

We utilized the Gaia Data Release 3 (DR3) to classify compact stellar systems (CSSs) into four categories: globular clusters, dwarf galaxies, dwarf spheroidals, and dwarf irregulars. This study employed a machine learning approach using a Random Forest classifier, which was trained on a sample of 1,000 CSSs selected from the Gaia Early Data Release 3 (EDR3). The input features included the CSSs' mean magnitudes in Gaia's six color bands (Gp, G, GR, RG, G, G, G, G, G, G, G, G, G, G, G, G, G, G, G, G, G, G, G, G, G, G, G, G, G, G, G, G, G, G, G, G, G, G, G, G, G, G, G, G, G, G, G, G, G, G, G, G, G, G, G, G, G, G, G, G, G, G, G, G, G, G, G, G, G, G, G, G, G, G, G, G, G, G, G, G, G, G, G, G, G, G, G, G, G, G, G, G, G, G, G, G, G

Simulations are a potent instrument for the development of Recommender Systems (RSs), enabling the assessment of algorithms under controlled conditions and the exploration of diverse scenarios. This paper introduces a framework for simulating RSs that leverages the existing ecosystem of recommender systems evaluation tools. By utilizing the standard, simulation results can be generated to inform decision-making processes. The authors present a prototype implementation of this framework, which is accessible at the provided URL.

Truncated sample means offer a robust approach for hypothesis testing regarding distributions with infinite variance or mean, as they remain well-defined and estimable even when the true population mean or variance is not finite. This paper introduces a test grounded in truncated sample means designed to detect shifts in location within such heavy-tailed populations. The study derives the test's asymptotic properties, establishes rejection regions that do not depend on unknown parameters, and formulates a rejection criterion based solely on the estimated quantile of the null distribution. The findings indicate that this test achieves high statistical power and maintains strong robustness against deviations from the null hypothesis.

Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) have demonstrated significant potential in processing Electroencephalography (EEG) data for Brain-Computer Interfaces (BCIs). However, CNNs suffer from a lack of interpretability and a high susceptibility to overfitting, particularly when dealing with the limited data typical of BCI applications. To address these challenges, this study introduces a novel framework that integrates the explainability of Graph Signal Processing (GSP) with the feature selection capabilities of the Lasso algorithm. The proposed method first employs GSP to model the EEG data as a graph, then utilizes a Lasso-based approach to identify the most informative nodes. Experimental results indicate that this framework surpasses existing state-of-the-art methods in terms of classification accuracy. Furthermore, the selected nodes can be leveraged to interpret the underlying physiological signals, offering a degree of interpretability that traditional CNNs lack.

This study examines how the $AdS/CFT$ correspondence applies to a massive scalar field within a noncommutative space, utilizing a holographic framework. We investigate the dynamics of a massive scalar field in the bulk $AdS$ space, which corresponds to a free, massive scalar operator in the boundary field theory. By analyzing the two-point correlation function of this operator, we determine its momentum-space spectral density. Our findings indicate that the noncommutative nature of the space influences the spectral density through a modification of the dispersion relation, which alters the relationship between the field's mass and its momentum.

We introduce a Markov Decision Process (MDP) framework for a kidney transplant system that accounts for the incompatibility of both patients and donors, a factor omitted in prior MDP analyses. By treating incompatibility as a distinct state variable, the model enables a more rigorous examination of transplant acceptance policies. We demonstrate that incorporating this element renders the resulting optimal policy significantly more complex. Furthermore, we establish that the Kolmogorov-Smirnov (K-S) test is applicable to evaluate the performance of acceptance criteria under this enhanced model.

Both Hidden Markov Models (HMMs) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks serve as foundational frameworks for modeling temporal sequences. Although HMMs utilize discrete hidden states and LSTMs rely on continuous recurrent neural networks, this study reveals that their latent representations are surprisingly similar. By demonstrating that HMMs can be approximated as RNNs, we establish a theoretical link between these two architectures. Furthermore, we prove that specific HMM configurations can be represented by extremely simple LSTMs, characterized by just a single hidden unit and linear gating mechanisms. These findings offer new perspectives on the intrinsic relationship between probabilistic sequence models and recurrent neural networks.

This study examines the compactness and membership in weighted Bergman space composition operators within the Schatten class of a pair of weighted Bergman spaces. Additionally, we establish a characterization for the ideal of hyper-composition operators within the Schatten class on two weighted Bergman spaces.

This study presents a novel approach to compressing transformer-based language models by employing a hybrid strategy that combines knowledge distillation with pruning. We evaluated this method on text classification tasks using the RoBERTa model across three datasets: SQuAD, GLUE, and the other GLUE benchmarks. Our findings indicate that the BERT-large-Base compressed architecture delivers the optimal balance between performance and efficiency.

The field of high-energy physics (HEP) is currently undergoing a historic transformation, driven by the massive scale of data produced by modern detectors and the increasing complexity of theoretical models. To keep pace with these developments, HEP must evolve by integrating data-driven methodologies and fostering closer collaboration with the broader data science community. This paper introduces the concept of "data scientists in HEP" and outlines a strategic roadmap for their integration. We propose establishing specific positions dedicated to data science within major HEP institutions, with the goal of modernizing data analysis, refining software infrastructure, and advancing tool development. Additionally, the document advocates for targeted initiatives designed to cultivate the next generation of HEP data scientists.

We define generalized curves of Howe and demonstrate their connection to composite Richelot isogenies. Furthermore, we extend the concept of elliptic curve decomposition to isogenies with degree $p^2$, where $p$ is a prime number. This extension establishes a correspondence between decomposed Richelot isogenies of degree $p^2$ and generalized curves of degree $p^2$. We also present a method to construct such curves by utilizing isogenies with degree $p^2$.

We report the discovery of three new magnetic hot subdwarfs, designated as V355 And, V356 And, and V357 And, within the V355–V357 Andromedae group. These objects were identified through a systematic survey of the V355–V357 Andromedae region using the 2.5-meter Hale Telescope at Palomar Observatory. Our analysis of the resulting spectra reveals that all three stars exhibit strong magnetic fields, with inferred surface magnetic field strengths ($B_{\rm surf}$) ranging from 10 to 150 kG. Furthermore, we determined the fundamental physical properties of these stars, including their masses, radii, and effective temperatures, by modeling their spectral energy distributions. Notably, the observed hydrogen abundances for these magnetic hot subdwarfs are approximately 0.1 dex lower than current theoretical models predict. This finding suggests that the nuclear reaction rates for the CNO cycle may be underestimated by roughly 10%.

This work introduces a methodology leveraging invariant matrix theory to analyze errors arising when approximating matrices with specific structures, such as Toeplitz, Hankel, or banded matrices, by linear combinations of matrices from a distinct set. The approach is demonstrated using the example of Hankel matrix approximation via sums of symmetric positive definite (SPD) matrices. In this scenario, we examine the error metric $E = E(A, \hat{A}) = \|A - \hat{A}\|_F$, where $\hat{A}$ represents the constructed approximation. We derive $E$ as the square root of a sum of squares (SOS) of the singular values of $E$, thereby enabling the application of invariant matrix theory to this problem. Furthermore, we provide a concrete instance of this analysis and discuss its implications for applications in scientific computing.

Wikipedia is a vast, continuously updated repository of freely accessible articles, with every page built using HTML combined with wikitext—a syntax that allows editors to add structure and formatting. While the final rendered pages display the same content to users regardless of whether they are viewed as HTML or raw wikitext, the underlying wikitext often contains supplementary information absent from the rendered output. This study analyzes the discrepancies between HTML-rendered versions and raw wikitext to determine if the latter holds unique insights. We examined link counts, link text, and the external websites referenced by these links. Our findings reveal that raw wikitext includes more links than the resulting HTML, yet the distribution of link targets remains consistent across both formats. Additionally, we discovered that the specific wording of anchor text varies between the two representations.

The magnetic properties of twisted bilayers, which feature a moiré superlattice, are examined using a tight-binding model. This model incorporates the interplay between the two layers' individual magnetizations and the resulting magnetic anisotropy. We identify a novel type of polar domain wall, which arises from a 36° shift in the moiré structure and exhibits a distinct triangular profile. These domain walls serve as a promising avenue for advancing topological physics.

This study examines how light travels in a static, spherically symmetric, perfect fluid universe characterized by a constant equation of state. We derive the geodesic equations and calculate the impact of gravity on photon paths. By contrasting this with light propagation in a flat universe, we identify significant physical differences. Furthermore, we analyze the shadow cast by the fluid body on surrounding photon trajectories, revealing distinct variations in its size and form compared to the standard black hole shadow.

We investigate the movement of a single colloid within a liquid crystal medium confined between a wavy wall and a flat boundary. The wavy wall features an alternating pattern of hills and wells, which creates corresponding variations in the local layer thickness. We demonstrate that, within the framework of the lubrication approximation, this configuration generates a localized force field capable of directing colloid trajectories. Furthermore, we examine the influence of various parameters on particle motion, including wall amplitude, the distance between the parallel plates, and the colloid's position relative to the wall.

The Roche limit defines the proximity within which a celestial body's self-gravity cannot counteract a primary body's tidal forces, leading to disintegration. This study examines the minimum Roche limit for a spherical asteroid with a density of 2,500 kg/m³ orbiting a 100 km diameter, 1000 km diameter, 10000 km diameter, 100000 km diameter, 1000000 km diameter, 10000000 km diameter, 100000000 km diameter, 1000000000 km diameter, 10000000000 km diameter, 100000000000 km diameter, 1000000000000 km diameter, 10000000000000 km diameter, 100000000000000 km diameter, 1000000000000000 km diameter, 10000000000000000 km diameter, 100000000000000000 km diameter, 1000000000

This study introduces a hybrid framework combining machine learning (ML) and quantum computing (QC) to enhance the efficiency of molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. By leveraging the computational power of both ML and QC, the approach targets the identification of rare conformational transitions and the characterization of specific molecular states. We illustrate this method using a simplified model system representing a peptide, where the primary objective is to detect the transition between two distinct states. To achieve this, we employ variational quantum circuits (VQCs) to generate a quantum state representing the system's configuration. Subsequently, a quantum circuit is designed to transition the system from one state to another, with the resulting quantum state serving as input for a supervised ML model trained to predict the system's configuration. This ML model effectively identifies the specific conformational changes associated with the transition. Finally, we validate the proposed ML-QC framework by comparing its performance against classical MD simulations, demonstrating that our method successfully captures the essential characteristics of the peptide's conformational transitions.

The MAPPIES code, a newly developed Monte-Carlo tool, enables the generation of polarized X-ray and gamma-ray spectra from various sources. It facilitates the creation of polarized spectra for diverse emission mechanisms, including synchrotron, bremsstrahlung, and Compton processes, and incorporates polarization effects from line emission, such as those originating from electron-positron annihilation. The software is designed to handle arbitrary viewing angles and source geometries, allowing for the simulation of detector responses to polarized photons. Additionally, it supports the modeling of instrumental polarization within detectors.

This study examines the impact of open water on the seasonal development of sea-ice thickness category (ITC) distributions in the Arctic Ocean. We introduce a novel, computationally efficient method to simulate this by defining the open water ITC distribution as a linear combination of the seasonal distributions observed in the marginal ice zone (MIM). We demonstrate that this approach accurately replicates the seasonal evolution of the average ITC distribution across the Arctic Ocean. Furthermore, we show that this method can be utilized to investigate the influence of open water on the seasonal progression of ITC distributions. Our findings reveal that the inclusion of open water accelerates the rate at which ITC distributions evolve during the summer season.

This study examines the Hermitian curve coverings defined by $X_{a,b,n,s}$ and $Y_{n,s}$, which are derived from the canonical $n$-fold and $s$-fold coverings of $\mathbb{P}^1$, respectively. We demonstrate that these curves possess distinct properties, implying they belong to different equivalence classes under curve isomorphism. Furthermore, we establish that the genus of both families adheres to the formula $(n+1)(h-1)$, where $h$ represents a parameter related to the degree of the covering map.

Singing voice synthesis has evolved significantly over the past decade, yet it remains an unresolved problem with substantial potential for both academic inquiry and commercial deployment. This paper presents a novel singing voice synthesis framework based on the WaveNet architecture. We introduce a dual-stream architecture designed to learn the melodic and rhythmic structures of music independently. Furthermore, we implement a novel attention mechanism to capture long-term temporal dependencies within the model. Experimental results indicate that our method outperforms existing state-of-the-art techniques.

This paper introduces NIPS4Bplus, an enhanced version of the NIPS4B bird song dataset, featuring recordings from 120 distinct species captured across 12 diverse habitats in Italy. We also present a novel ecoacoustic application for this resource, demonstrating how it can support bird population monitoring and the assessment of ecosystem health. To facilitate this, we propose a novel metric called the Bird Activity Index (BAI), which quantifies avian presence by measuring the temporal density of bird calls. We evaluate the proposed BAI using the NIPS4Bplus data and compare it with an established metric, the Ecoacoustic Index (EI). Our findings indicate that BAI exhibits a stronger correlation with actual bird call density than EI does. Furthermore, we demonstrate the utility of BAI in monitoring bird populations within a real-world scenario involving a forest in Tuscany, Italy.

Event cameras offer a compelling alternative to frame-based sensors, featuring high temporal resolution and a dynamic range that far exceeds conventional systems. However, these advantages are often hindered by event camera calibration challenges. This paper introduces a novel calibration framework for event cameras that facilitates extrinsic calibration between frame-based and event-based sensors, as well as intrinsics calibration for the cameras themselves. The approach utilizes a 3D model of scene geometry to simulate the rendering of events, thereby circumventing the need for specialized calibration targets. The method's efficacy is demonstrated through both synthetic experiments and real-world scenarios.

Graph learning has proven effective in numerous scenarios, including social networks, e-commerce platforms, knowledge graphs, and biological data. However, existing research predominantly relies on labeled data, which is often scarce or unavailable in real-world applications. To address this, we introduce a new framework for unsupervised graph learning that utilizes self-supervised learning to generate pseudo-labels for training. Specifically, we employ a graph autoencoder to create node embeddings and use a contrastive learning approach to derive training samples from these representations. Experimental results demonstrate that our method outperforms current state-of-the-art unsupervised graph learning techniques.
The action of the four-strand braid group on exceptional collections within the degree 2 Hirzebruch surface is represented as a linear application on an associated Cayley graph.

This study introduces a 3D guidance system for retinal surgery that utilizes a spotlight projector to create a depth map of the retina. By analyzing the shift in the spot's position, the system calculates the distance of retinal surface points from the probe tip, thereby offering surgeons a visual representation of the retinal topography. This approach eliminates the need for complex 3D reconstruction, which is particularly advantageous in the context of the eye's limited depth of field. Furthermore, the proposed method can be adapted for other surgical procedures where the probe tip is visible.
We expand the $F$-product formula into a corresponding summation formula.

The FIDO2 standard, which is gaining significant traction, aims to drive the adoption of passwordless authentication. This paper introduces a novel method for generating a secret key that is derived from a user's voice, thereby facilitating passwordless login through voice biometrics. The key generation process leverages the distinctive acoustic features of the user's voice, ensuring that the resulting voice biometric key is unique to the individual. Additionally, the research outlines a framework for evaluating the entropy of voice biometric keys, which serves as a metric for assessing the key generation's randomness and its capacity to withstand brute-force attacks. Finally, the study analyzes the entropy levels of the generated keys to demonstrate their suitability for use as cryptographic secrets.

We demonstrate that a novel Weyl-Wigner approach, which maps qubit states onto a unit sphere, fails to capture fundamental aspects of quantum physics. Specifically, it cannot model the Bloch sphere's surface dynamics, nor can it represent the complete set of qubit states.

This paper introduces a novel interface for video applications that enhances the user's sense of control through an innovative, dynamic, and interactive visual summary. By enabling users to adjust the playback speed of the summary, the system provides a comprehensive view of the content. The interface is built upon a timeline that integrates keyframes, textual labels, and progress indicators, offering a flexible and customizable experience. The system employs a hybrid approach combining supervised and unsupervised learning to generate the visual summary. Specifically, the summary generation utilizes a pretrained video model alongside a custom CNN trained on a dataset of 1,000 manually labeled videos. The interface's timeline is populated with a mix of user-controlled elements and system-generated ones, including adjustable speed segments, manually selected keyframes, and automatically detected scene transitions.

This work examines the expressive power of the $\pi$-calculus, focusing on its ability to define behaviors that reactive Turing machines cannot. We demonstrate that every reactive Turing machine process can be translated into an equivalent $\pi$-calculus process, while also characterizing the specific $\pi$-calculus constructs essential for this equivalence. Furthermore, we show that $\pi$-messages must be restricted to a specific subset of all possible types to achieve this result. We also reveal that reactive Turing machines can model $\pi$-calculus input/output actions, except for the creation of new channel names. We conclude by contrasting the two formalisms regarding their capacity to specify behavior: unlike reactive Turing machines, $\pi$-calculus is capable of describing the finite-executable behavior of certain systems.

We introduce a novel, designed Gray code for ordered trees, where each successive representation corresponds to a tree derived from the previous one via a single rotation operation. This code adheres to a lexicographic ordering of the trees. Our construction is built upon a specific variant of the standard subtree ordering method, which had been previously utilized to create a stack-sortable permutation Gray code.

Reconstructing particle trajectories in high-energy physics is essential for determining their physical properties. This process involves identifying tracks within noisy, high-multiplicity environments, such as those found in heavy-ion collisions, and linking them to corresponding hits in the tracking detector. This work presents a new methodology for track reconstruction in heavy-ion collisions, utilizing the Deep Learning framework of the FastTrack algorithm. We evaluate the method's performance by comparing it against the standard ATLAS track reconstruction pipeline. The results demonstrate that the Deep Learning approach achieves superior efficiency and lower computational costs, particularly in scenarios with high background noise.

This study introduces a novel time-discontinuous prismatic space-time finite-element approach for simulating free-surface flows. The method employs a standard prismatic space framework in the three spatial dimensions while utilizing a distinct, higher-order polynomial basis for the time dimension. This design allows the finite elements to adapt seamlessly to variable time-marching steps, ensuring that the resulting mesh aligns with individual time intervals. By integrating these elements, the technique effectively resolves common challenges associated with standard finite elements in Lagrangian space-time simulations, such as difficulties with free-surface boundary conditions and the handling of moving boundaries. The proposed method is validated through a series of numerical experiments, including the simulation of a plunging cylinder, a breaking wave, and a breaking wave group.

A circular $k$-flow refers to a circular $k$-flow defined on signed graphs. We demonstrate that circular $k$-flows exist for signed graphs with a maximum degree of 3, provided $k$ is either 4 or an odd integer greater than or equal to 5. Furthermore, we establish that the presence of a circular $k$-flow corresponds to modulo $k$-orientation for signed graphs satisfying specific conditions.

This study addresses the Modular Subset Sum problem, which involves determining if a target value $t$ can be expressed as a linear combination of $n$ integers $a_1, \ldots, a_n$ and a modulus $m$ with coefficients from $\{0, 1\}$. We present a deterministic algorithm running in $O(n + m)$ time, improving upon the prior best result of $O(nm)$. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the problem can be solved in $2^{\tilde{O}(n^{1/3})}$ time, surpassing the previous state-of-the-art bound of $2^{\tilde{O}(\sqrt{n})}$.

This study investigates the variability of M-dwarf stars within the Kepler field, utilizing a dataset of 1,000 rotational variable stars (RVs) identified by the Kepler pipeline. By analyzing the light curves of these stars, we determined their rotation periods and flare frequencies. We then compared these findings against a control sample of 1,000 non-variable stars to identify the characteristics of flaring stars. Our results indicate that flaring stars are more prevalent among later M-type dwarfs and exhibit a distinct difference from non-flaring RVs: flaring stars display a higher frequency of rotational variations. Additionally, we examined the relationship between spectral type and flare frequency, revealing that stars with spectral types later than M6 exhibit a higher flare frequency than those earlier than M6. Finally, we analyzed the relationship between rotation period and flare frequency, finding that flaring stars with rotation periods exceeding 10 days have a higher flare frequency than those with shorter periods.

In the study of the Dictyostelium cellular model, the influence of LanB1 and SCAR mutants on hemocyte motility was examined. The findings indicate that the co-presence of these mutants significantly enhances movement speed, a phenomenon attributed to the increased turnover of actin filaments.

We introduce c-siam, a novel architecture for extracting linguistic information from speech. c-siam employs a self-supervised approach to pre-train a speaker- and content-aware joint encoder, utilizing a contrastive loss function. This pre-training phase leverages speaker labels and phoneme content from the LibriLight dataset. Subsequently, the model is fine-tuned on the TIMIT dataset for word graph generation. Our approach surpasses prior work by achieving a 2.4% reduction in Word Error Rate (WER) and a 19.3% reduction in insertion error rate.

This study introduces a refined version of the model presented in arXiv:2007.11803, which describes neutrino-nucleon total and partial cross sections for charged-current interactions on protons and neutrons at energies ranging from 10 GeV to 100 TeV. The enhanced model demonstrates superior alignment with experimental data on neutrino-nucleon total cross sections and exhibits reduced discrepancies with recent measurements of partial cross sections. Theoretical predictions are benchmarked against existing experimental data, as well as other theoretical frameworks, with a specific focus on the recent results from the FOCUS collaboration.

This study addresses the stabilization of linear time-varying stochastic systems driven by linear dynamics, stochastic white noise, and an unknown order of hidden Markov chains. The proposed control scheme employs a two-stage methodology: first, a data-driven approach estimates the unknown Markov chain and system dynamics; second, these estimates are utilized to design a stabilizing controller. The analysis demonstrates that the control algorithm ensures almost sure stabilization, with the closed-loop system's ergodic behavior converging to the desired target system. Furthermore, the work establishes a law of large numbers for the closed-loop system, confirming that its long-term time average aligns closely with the expected behavior of the deterministic counterpart.

This paper introduces BTAI, a novel Behavior Tree (BT) architecture designed to enhance the adaptability of planning within Reinforcement Learning (RL) environments. By leveraging a tree structure, BTAI offers superior interpretability and generalization compared to RL methods, while its flexible architecture allows for the integration of diverse planners. However, existing BT-based approaches often struggle with task completion time and success rates. To address these limitations, we propose BTAI, which employs a Bayesian Tree Architecture to dynamically select the most suitable BT node based on the current state. This mechanism enables the system to adapt to varying conditions and optimize performance. Experimental results demonstrate that BTAI surpasses its predecessors in both success rates and completion times. Furthermore, it exhibits robust generalization capabilities, successfully transferring learned behaviors to previously unseen environments.

This study derives the Korteweg-de Vries equation from the hydrodynamic equations describing the quark-gluon plasma, demonstrating that the resulting solitary wave solutions are highly sensitive to the equation of state. We examine the impact of varying equation of state parameters on the amplitude and width of these soliton waves, concluding that the derived single wave solutions align with experimental observations of heavy-ion collisions.

Furthermore, the linear Eberlein-Grothendieck property of the dual of an arbitrary locally total space is characterized. We establish a method to generate formal power series related to the isochrony center for a Hamiltonian system, which effectively yields formal Taylor series for the Hamiltonian function under its own desingularization process. This approach provides a fresh perspective on linking Taylor coefficients of the Hamiltonian function to the phenomenon of isochronicity.

This study examines the existence and stability of periodic orbits in the Lorenz system. By applying the Melnikov method, we derive the existence of periodic solutions with specific periods, categorized as $2n$ for $n \geq 1$, $2n+1$, and $2n+3$ for $n \geq 1$. Furthermore, we establish sufficient conditions for the stability of these orbits. Finally, we demonstrate that the set of periods associated with these periodic solutions constitutes a relatively dense set within the positive integers.

This work examines the application of Malliavin calculus within a broad class of statistical frameworks, including those with infinite-variability. We establish upper bounds for the derivatives of log-likelihood functions, utilizing the Poincaré inequality and the Herbst argument. Furthermore, we demonstrate the convergence rates of the corresponding Maximum Likelihood Estimators (MLEs) in both $L^1$ and $L^2$ norms.

We examine the spectrum of unitary representations for the universal Teichmüller space equipped with the Schottli group, defined via the Laplacian on the associated Teichmüller space. Our findings indicate that the critical exponents associated with these representations correlate with the spectrum of the Laplacian on this space. Furthermore, we investigate the behavior of these representations near the identity element, demonstrating that they constitute a family of tempered representations.

Fourier transforms are widely used in time-series prediction, yet they are typically designed for static signals, overlooking the dynamic nature of evolving data. We introduce the autoregressive Fourier transform (ARFT), a method that models time-series evolution by applying a time-dependent autoregressive process to the frequency coefficients. We demonstrate that this approach is highly effective for time-series forecasting, particularly in domains where historical data is scarce. ARFT achieves performance comparable to state-of-the-art methods while using significantly fewer parameters.

This study investigates the viability of the $f(R,T)$ gravity model, specifically $f(R,T)=R+2\epsilon T$, within the framework of a flat Friedmann-Lemaître-Robertson-Walker (FLRW) universe. We analyze the model's consistency with observational data by examining the evolution of the equation of state and energy densities for matter and dark energy. Furthermore, we assess the model against the SNeIa dataset, the combined dataset of SNeIa and Baryon Acoustic Oscillations (BAO), and the Pantheon sample. Our results indicate that the model remains compatible with these observations, provided the parameter $\epsilon$ is sufficiently small.

This study addresses the resource allocation for service function chains (SFCs) within Multi-access Edge Computing (MEC) environments. The primary objective is to minimize the total service latency for all SFCs by optimizing the assignment of SFCs to available MEC nodes and the distribution of computational resources. This challenge is decomposed into two subproblems: SFC assignment and resource allocation. The SFC assignment problem is formulated as a bipartite graph matching task, solved using the Hungarian algorithm. The resource allocation problem is modeled as a linear programming issue, tackled via the Simplex method. The proposed solution is proven to be optimal. Simulation results demonstrate that the achieved latency reduction is superior to that of existing methods.

We investigate the renormalization group flow of a two-dimensional Dirac fermion system coupled to a U(1) gauge field, incorporating both disorder and finite density. By applying the $\epsilon$-expansion method around three dimensions, we demonstrate that disorder renders fixed points unstable. Furthermore, we identify a reentrant phase transition that occurs as the finite chemical potential increases.

This research investigates the life events of individuals with depression compared to control users, utilizing data from a large-scale social media study. By leveraging publicly available event labels, we demonstrate that depressive individuals report a higher frequency of positive events compared to controls, whereas controls experience a greater number of negative events. Furthermore, our findings indicate that positive events have a more substantial impact on depression than negative ones do with controls. These results highlight the significant role that social media-derived life events play in understanding depression and offer valuable insights for developing novel interventions.

We investigate the possibility that a QCD-like theory, characterized by a light scalar glueball, accounts for dark matter. By analyzing the scalar gluebar's phenomenology, we demonstrate that it can satisfy the requirements of dark matter candidates, including stability, the correct relic density, and alignment with current direct detection limits.

Na$_{4-\delta}$NiTeO$_{6}$ is a three-dimensional triangular-lattice antiferromagnet characterized by a reduced Ni$^{2+}$ magnetic moment of 0.2 $\mu_{\rm{B}}$, a marked reduction from the spin-only value of 2.0 $\mu_{\rm{B}}$. This study investigates the impact of the crystalline electric field on the Ni$^{2+}$ magnetic moment using neutron diffraction and polarized neutron powder scattering. The analysis reveals that the crystalline electric field significantly reduces the Ni$^{2+}$ magnetic moment by approximately 0.8 $\mu_{\rm{B}}$, leaving an orbital contribution of only 0.2 $\mu_{\rm{B}}$. This finding indicates that the Ni$^{2+}$ magnetic moment in Na$_{4-\delta}$NiTeO$_{6}$ is primarily driven by spin angular momentum rather than orbital effects.

In large-scale distributed systems like the Internet of Things, trust is essential for making decisions. However, the sheer volume of data generated by these devices makes it difficult to manually identify and aggregate the necessary information for trust assessments. To address this, we introduce a framework for the automatic discovery and unification of data sources used in trust evaluation. This approach utilizes a data mining technique called association rule learning to identify patterns in data, thereby revealing relationships between different sources. The framework is designed to be adaptable, allowing users to customize it for specific applications by defining criteria for source relevance and reliability. The methodology is demonstrated through a case study involving the automatic discovery and unification of data sources for assessing the trustworthiness of IoT devices.

Cubic splines are extensively utilized for data interpolation and smoothing, particularly in fields like geosciences and medicine. However, in certain applications, it is vital to maintain data monotonicity, which conventional splines often fail to do. This paper introduces a new algorithm designed to generate piecewise cubic splines that accurately reflect the monotonicity of the underlying data. By ensuring monotonicity, the algorithm also maintains key properties such as continuity, continuity of derivatives, and data interpolation. The method is designed to be straightforward to implement and computationally efficient. We demonstrate its effectiveness through various examples, including synthetic datasets, real-world data, and practical applications.

This study examines exact black bounces within the frameworks of de Sitter and anti-de Sitter spacetimes. We demonstrate that while de Sitter geometries transition between distinct configurations upon varying the equation of state parameter, anti-de Sitter geometries maintain a static configuration regardless of changes to this parameter.

This study introduces a pioneering approach for automatically classifying and labeling varied audio recordings. We developed a feature extraction and classification framework based on spectrograms, employing a ResNet-based Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) to train the classifier. The trained model was applied to categorize and tag a diverse dataset of 1,000 audio clips, capturing a wide variety of real-world sounds. The dataset was split into 80% training and 20% validation sets, with the model trained on the former and evaluated using the latter. The results demonstrate that CNNs are effective for audio classification and that the proposed method successfully generates high-quality audio annotations.

The stability of diversity is a fundamental issue in both ecology and biochemical networks, where it is widely recognized that fluctuations in individual species populations can undermine overall diversity stability. This study examines the relationship between diversity stability and the thermodynamic properties of the underlying chemical reaction system. We demonstrate that the thermodynamic potential of such a system is capable of predicting the stability of its diversity. Furthermore, we establish a stability criterion applicable to the thermodynamic potential within a broad class of these systems. Utilizing this criterion, we identify conditions under which diversity remains stable.

This study examines the evolution of a network following the deletion of a single node, utilizing the avalanche size to quantify the extent of structural disintegration. We introduce a novel method for characterizing the critical behavior of such systems by analyzing the probability distribution of these avalanches. Our analysis demonstrates that the resulting critical exponents align with those observed in standard avalanche phenomena within scale-free networks. Furthermore, we establish a direct correlation between avalanche magnitude and the degree of network fragmentation.

While discourse-level understanding is essential for human communication, constructing holistic models remains difficult because of the vast number of possible discourse structures. This paper introduces a novel approach to modeling holistic discourse comprehension through a two-stage process. First, we develop a lightweight, high-efficiency method to identify the primary discourse structure, followed by the application of a structure-aware model for semantic role labeling. This strategy significantly enhances the efficiency of discourse modeling and achieves a 2.4% improvement in F1 scores for semantic role labeling.

This paper details the creation of a PML implementation for the FEM-based Pseudospectral Method (PSM) designed for seismic wave propagation. The approach employs a complex-valued formulation, where the complex-valued PML (CPML) is incorporated by adjusting the system's matrix coefficients to ensure stability. The study evaluates the PML's performance on both 1D and 3D models, including a 1D setup with a complex velocity profile and a 3D scenario involving a complex-valued velocity model. Results demonstrate that the current implementation achieves up to 99% reduction in energy leakage within the PML layer. Consequently, computational resources required for the PML are merely 1% of those needed for a perfectly absorbing medium.

The study of droplet interactions, a critical component of multiphase flows, has been extensively examined using the volume-of-fluid (VOF) method. This research introduces a novel "butterfly" type breakup mechanism, which occurs when a droplet collides with a liquid film and rebounds. The authors present a new VOF-based simulation of this phenomenon, utilizing a high-order VOF scheme integrated with a level-set method to enhance interface resolution. The simulation results, which align closely with experimental data, reveal that the rebounding process is driven by the formation of a liquid bridge. This bridge generates a complex flow field characterized by a vortex pair and a central cavity, both of which play pivotal roles in the breakup. The interaction between these vortices and the central cavity is identified as the primary cause of the "butterfly" breakup. The authors further propose a new breakup criterion that incorporates the Weber number and the ratio of the rebounding droplet's diameter to the liquid bridge's diameter. This criterion effectively predicts the onset of breakup, demonstrating strong agreement with experimental observations.

The rapid proliferation of the Internet of Things (IoT) has driven the need for traffic management systems that are both efficient and scalable. This paper introduces a novel solution leveraging Software-Defined Networking (SDN) to optimize IoT traffic handling. By utilizing centralized SDN controllers, the system dynamically manages traffic flows, thereby reducing network congestion and enhancing overall performance. The proposed approach employs a centralized architecture where the controller allocates specific network paths for different device categories based on their traffic requirements. Furthermore, the system incorporates a traffic classification module that categorizes IoT devices into three tiers—high, medium, and low—according to their bandwidth consumption. Consequently, high-priority devices are routed through premium network segments to ensure minimal latency, while medium and low-priority devices are assigned to more congested areas. The system's effectiveness is validated through simulations using the Ryu controller, with results demonstrating that the proposed method significantly outperforms traditional routing strategies in terms of both efficiency and scalability.

The architecture of a protoplanetary disk is governed by the planet's mass and orbit shape. This study investigates how the disk responds to a planet with a highly elliptical orbit, utilizing a simplified model of the planet-disk interaction. We demonstrate that the disk's response is dictated by the planet's orbital period and the disk's viscous timescale. Specifically, the disk's reaction to the varying gravitational forces of the planet's orbit is contingent on the ratio between these two timescales. When the viscous timescale is shorter than the orbital period, the disk reacts to the varying forces, resulting in a disk structure that mirrors the planet's orbit. Conversely, when the viscous timescale exceeds the orbital period, the disk reacts only to the time-averaged gravitational potential, producing a structure that does not resemble the orbit. We further explore the implications of these findings for the formation of eccentric planetary orbits.

This study examines the theoretical and practical characteristics of embedding algorithms within Euclidean, hyperbolic, and positive definite matrix spaces. We introduce a novel algorithm capable of embedding symmetric positive definite matrices into a Euclidean space while preserving geodesic relationships, and we demonstrate that this method maintains metric properties inherent to the matrix data. Our findings indicate that, across various practical applications, models utilizing these matrix spaces are competitive with, and often superior to, those based on standard Euclidean or hyperbolic spaces.

The hydrogen backbone required for the European Union's 2050 net-zero emissions goal can be largely built using repurposed natural gas infrastructure. This paper examines the most efficient strategies for integrating new and existing pipelines to connect hydrogen production hubs with major demand centers. We model the network expansion challenge as a Minimum Steiner Tree problem, incorporating a set of additional Steiner points to minimize total costs. We introduce a novel branch-and-cut algorithm that leverages flow-based polyhedral theory to solve this variation effectively. Computational results indicate that the method can solve instances involving up to 20 demand centers and 15 Steiner points optimally. Furthermore, we analyze the impact of natural gas pipeline repurposing timing on the final network design and evaluate the efficacy of various heuristics for generating high-quality upper bounds.

This study introduces a novel technique for determining the surface magnetic field of a Sun-like star by analyzing the circular polarization spectrum of its photosphere. The method relies on the assumption that the surface magnetic field vector is aligned with the subsurface field vector. By applying this approach to the G2V star HD 173416, we derived a surface magnetic field of 1.25$\pm$0.05 kG, which aligns closely with the subsurface field's azimuth of 1.27 kG. This agreement supports the hypothesis that the surface field is parallel to the subsurface field. Furthermore, we calculated the subsurface field's inclination angle to be 6.2$^\circ$ relative to the surface. We introduce a new mechanism for generating squeezed light within integrated photonic systems by leveraging topological phases. This approach utilizes a specific interaction between topological modes and a squeezed vacuum state to induce parametric squeezing exclusively in the topological component. Consequently, this method offers a distinct alternative to conventional techniques for generating topologically protected optical modes, enabling the concurrent production of both.

This paper introduces a trajectory planning approach designed to optimize the flight time of drones by minimizing the magnitude of acceleration. The method is developed by modeling the relationship between velocity and time, where the acceleration is minimized by reducing the sum of the squares of the third derivatives of these variables. The resulting optimization problem is solved using a gradient descent technique. The proposed approach is evaluated against polynomial methods, demonstrating superior time-optimality. The paper further discusses the method's applicability to scenarios involving drone swarms.

This study establishes a recursive formula to count $ \mathbb{F}_q $-linear one-additive conjugate codes for any specified length. Furthermore, it provides the number of $ \mathbb{F}_q $-linear self-conjugate codes and those with one-additive Hermitian self-conjugacy in the specific length $ q^{m}+1 $. Finally, it calculates the weights associated with codes falling under these specific classifications.

This paper examines the disparity between high-earning positions available to high-energy physics (HEP) physicists and the lower-than-expected salaries they receive. It investigates the root causes of this issue and outlines strategies to enhance physicist-to-industry career transitions, with a specific focus on leveraging connections with alumni.

The angular separation between the $b$-quark from a top quark decay and a jet originating directly from $W$ boson decay serves as a sensitive probe for $W$ polarization. This study examines how such an angle behaves across various top quark decay chains, specifically those involving on-shell versus off-shell $W$ bosons. It is demonstrated that the peak position of the angle's distribution reflects the polarization state of the $W$ and distinguishes between scenarios where the $W$ is fully polarized and fully unpolarized. This angular variable offers a robust method for analyzing $W$ polarization within the framework of effective field theory, as it can constrain both dimensionful and dimensionless operators. Furthermore, the analysis evaluates the sensitivity of this angle to new physics effects, including top quark decays into off-shell $W$ bosons and the presence of a virtual $W$-Higgs mixing.

We introduce new sum rules for the $\xi$-moments of the leading-twist D-meson distribution amplitudes (DAs), derived from the corresponding $\xi$-moment sum rules of the D-meson's parent tetraquark D$_{s0}(2317)$, which is modeled as a D$\bar{u}s$ diquark-antidiquark state. These new sum rules provide an additional constraint on the D-meson DA parameters, allowing for a more precise extraction of the DA's shape. We further examine the sensitivity of the D-meson DA shape to the specific diquark configuration of the tetraquark state.

This work derives a novel relationship linking the $k$-th eigenvalues of a power hypergraph to those of its signed subgraphs, a finding that rectifies an earlier error in existing literature. We further establish the tightest possible upper bound for the $k$-th eigenvalues in a power hypergraph featuring a specific uniformity and size, alongside providing corresponding examples that demonstrate this sharpness.

This study introduces a novel method for estimating the positions of low Earth orbit satellites by utilizing intersatellite range and velocity data. The approach relies on a linearized orbital dynamics model, which is solved via a Kalman filter to generate position estimates. The paper details the model's formulation, presents simulation results, and evaluates the accuracy of the localization. The findings reveal that localization accuracy using only inter-satellite data is markedly inferior to that achieved by combining inter-satellite and ground station data. The work concludes by outlining potential applications of this technique in scenarios where ground stations are absent or compromised.

The orbital decay of the hot Jupiter XO-3b, driven by tidal interactions with its host star, has been observed over a span of 11 years. This study aims to refine the measurement of the orbital period decay rate, $\dot{P}_b$, by analyzing the transit times of the planet. We employed a novel approach that accounts for the correlated noise inherent in transit timing data, utilizing a Gaussian process (GP) model to characterize the stellar activity signal. Our findings indicate that the GP method yields a more precise estimate of $\dot{P}_b$ compared to traditional techniques. Specifically, our analysis results in an orbital period decay rate of $\dot{P}_b = (-1.01 \pm 0.15) \times 10^{-3}$ s yr$^{-1}$, which aligns with the value derived from previous studies.

We introduce a new calibration framework designed for astrophysical experiments that integrates Bayesian methods with machine learning. This approach employs a neural network to learn the mapping between raw detector signals and physical parameters, subsequently utilizing this network to estimate physical parameters directly from the raw data. To ensure the network's predictions remain reliable, we implement a strategy that combines the raw data-driven network with a standard, model-based calibration algorithm. This integration enables the network to learn calibration characteristics from the data while constraining its outputs using the established model. We evaluate the efficacy of this method using simulated data from the Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB), specifically from the Planck mission. Our results demonstrate that the proposed calibration framework successfully recovers the model-based calibration parameters with high accuracy. Furthermore, we show that employing this new method yields a significant reduction in the covariance of the CMB power spectrum compared to relying solely on traditional model-based techniques.

This work investigates the genus-zero equivariant Gromov-Witten theory of the projective bundle $\mathbb P(E)$ over a base $X$, where $E$ is a rank $r$ vector bundle equipped with a linear action from a torus $T$. The study assumes that the $T$-action on $X$ fixes a point and preserves the bundle $E$. The primary finding establishes a link between the equivariant GW theory of $\mathbb P(E)$ and that of $E$ itself, with the connection depending on the specific action of $T$ on $E$. Furthermore, we demonstrate that this relationship remains valid under logarithmic GW theory when considering targets with boundary divisors.

We investigate central values of antiautomorphic forms related to Rankin-Selberg L-functions for automorphic representations of $\mathrm{GL}_2$ over a totally real field, demonstrating that under appropriate hypotheses, these central elements do not vanish. Specifically, our framework extends the findings of the earlier work by the authors on Rankin-Selberg L-functions associated to two distinct $\mathrm{GL}_2$ representations over a totally real field, utilizing the analytic properties of the L-functions established by those previous studies.

Constrained longitudinal data analysis (C LDA) is a standard approach for continuous outcomes in longitudinal clinical trials, typically utilizing random effects models. However, these conventional models often fail to account for the non-linear trends that frequently characterize such data. This study introduces a novel C LDA framework based on natural cubic splines, which incorporates non-linearity into the analysis of continuous outcomes. The proposed spline model is compared against the traditional random effects model, along with two existing spline-based alternatives: a marginal model and a joint modeling approach. These comparisons were conducted using both simulated longitudinal datasets and a real dataset from a clinical trial involving multiple time points. Results indicate that the spline model yields superior performance in terms of bias, root mean squared error, and coverage probability, particularly when the sample size is small.

CRAWLING is a routing algorithm designed for mobile ad hoc networks (MANETs) that integrates the core mechanisms of AODV and DSDV while incorporating stochastic behaviors into its routing process. By introducing randomness, CRAWLING enhances network scalability and reduces the likelihood of routing loops. Its route discovery phase utilizes a route request (RREQ) packet, which is flooded throughout the network with a preference for nodes possessing the highest metric values, such as the lowest hop count. To introduce stochastic elements, a node may forward an RREQ to a neighbor with a slightly inferior metric with a specific probability. Similarly, during route establishment, the network relies on the highest metric neighbors to propagate route acknowledgments (RACKs) back to the sender, again allowing for probabilistic forwarding to neighbors with marginally lower metrics.
